title: Myocardial infarction
text: Myocardial infarction occurs when blood flow to part of the heart muscle is blocked, usually by a clot forming on a ruptured atherosclerotic plaque. Rapid reperfusion with angioplasty or thrombolytic drugs limits permanent damage to cardiac tissue.

title: Atherosclerosis
text: Atherosclerosis is the gradual build-up of cholesterol-rich plaque inside arterial walls, narrowing vessels and reducing blood supply. LDL cholesterol, hypertension and smoking accelerate the process.

title: BRCA1 and breast cancer
text: Inherited mutations in the BRCA1 gene sharply raise lifetime risk of breast and ovarian cancer because the protein normally repairs double-strand DNA breaks. Carriers are offered enhanced screening or preventive surgery.

title: Antibiotic resistance
text: Bacteria evolve resistance when antibiotics kill susceptible cells but leave mutants that survive and reproduce. Overuse of antibiotics in medicine and agriculture accelerates selection for resistant strains such as MRSA.

title: mRNA vaccines
text: mRNA vaccines deliver instructions for cells to produce a harmless viral protein, training the immune system to recognise the pathogen. Lipid nanoparticles protect the fragile mRNA and help it enter cells.

title: Type 2 diabetes and insulin resistance
text: In type 2 diabetes, tissues respond poorly to insulin, so glucose stays in the bloodstream. Weight loss, exercise and drugs such as metformin improve insulin sensitivity.

title: Sleep and memory
text: During deep sleep the brain replays recent experiences, consolidating them into long-term memory. Chronic sleep deprivation impairs attention and the formation of new memories.

title: Okapi BM25
text: BM25 is a ranking function that scores documents by query term frequency, inverse document frequency and document length normalisation. It remains a strong lexical baseline for search engines.

title: Dense passage retrieval
text: Dense retrieval encodes queries and documents into vectors with neural networks and finds nearest neighbours by cosine similarity. It captures synonyms and paraphrases that exact keyword matching misses.

title: Reciprocal rank fusion
text: Reciprocal rank fusion merges several ranked lists by summing 1 divided by a constant plus each document's rank. It needs no score calibration, which makes it popular for combining keyword and vector search.

title: Cross-encoder rerankers
text: A cross-encoder feeds the query and a candidate passage through a transformer together, producing a relevance score with full token-level attention. It is more accurate than a bi-encoder but too slow to score a whole corpus, so it is used to rerank a short list.

title: The transformer architecture
text: The transformer architecture relies on self-attention to relate every token in a sequence to every other token, enabling parallel training on large text corpora.

title: Gradient descent
text: Gradient descent minimises a loss function by repeatedly stepping in the direction of the negative gradient. The learning rate decides whether training converges or diverges.

title: Hash tables
text: A hash table maps keys to buckets using a hash function, giving average constant-time lookup, insertion and deletion. Collisions are handled by chaining or open addressing.

title: Inverted index
text: An inverted index maps each term to the list of documents containing it, letting search engines retrieve candidates without scanning every document.

title: The greenhouse effect
text: Greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane trap outgoing infrared radiation, warming the lower atmosphere. Burning fossil fuels has raised atmospheric CO2 by roughly half since the industrial revolution.

title: Sea level rise
text: Global sea level is rising as ocean water expands when heated and as glaciers and ice sheets melt. Coastal cities face more frequent flooding and saltwater intrusion.

title: Photosynthesis
text: Plants convert sunlight, water and carbon dioxide into glucose and oxygen in chloroplasts. The light reactions capture energy, and the Calvin cycle uses it to fix carbon.

title: CRISPR gene editing
text: CRISPR-Cas9 lets scientists cut DNA at a chosen location guided by an RNA sequence, enabling precise gene editing in cells and organisms.

title: Black holes
text: A black hole is a region of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape beyond the event horizon. They form when massive stars collapse.

title: Detecting exoplanets
text: Astronomers detect exoplanets by the tiny dip in starlight when a planet transits its star, or by the wobble of the star caused by orbiting planets.

title: Plate tectonics
text: Earth's lithosphere is split into plates that move slowly over the mantle. Earthquakes and volcanoes cluster at plate boundaries where plates collide, separate or slide past each other.

title: The gut microbiome
text: Trillions of bacteria in the human intestine help digest fibre, train the immune system and produce vitamins. Disruption of the microbiome has been linked to inflammatory bowel disease and obesity.

title: Alzheimer's disease
text: Alzheimer's disease is marked by amyloid plaques and tau tangles that destroy neurons, causing progressive memory loss. No treatment yet reverses the disease, though some drugs slow decline.

title: Hypertension
text: Chronic high blood pressure damages arteries and raises the risk of stroke, kidney disease and heart failure. Reducing salt, exercising and taking antihypertensive drugs lower the risk.

title: Statins
text: Statins lower LDL cholesterol by blocking an enzyme in the liver, reducing the risk of heart attacks and strokes in people with cardiovascular disease.

title: Overfitting in machine learning
text: A model overfits when it memorises training examples and performs poorly on new data. Regularisation, dropout and more training data reduce overfitting.

title: Approximate nearest neighbour search
text: Approximate nearest neighbour algorithms such as HNSW build navigable graphs so vector search stays fast on millions of embeddings, trading a little recall for large speedups.

title: Evaluating retrieval systems
text: Retrieval systems are evaluated with precision at k, recall and normalised discounted cumulative gain, which rewards placing highly relevant documents near the top of the ranking.

title: Quantum computing
text: Quantum computers use qubits that can be in superposition and entangled, allowing certain problems such as factoring to be solved faster than on classical machines.

title: Renewable energy
text: Solar panels and wind turbines generate electricity without burning fuel. Falling costs have made them the cheapest source of new power in many regions, though storage is needed for cloudy and windless periods.

title: Vitamin D
text: The skin makes vitamin D when exposed to sunlight. Deficiency weakens bones and has been associated with rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

title: Malaria
text: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes. Bed nets, insecticides and artemisinin-based drugs have cut deaths, but drug resistance is a growing threat.

title: Coral bleaching
text: When ocean temperatures rise, corals expel the symbiotic algae that give them colour and food, a process called bleaching. Prolonged bleaching kills reefs.

title: Large language models
text: Large language models are transformers trained to predict the next token on vast text datasets. Retrieval-augmented generation grounds their answers in documents fetched from a search index.

title: Stroke
text: A stroke occurs when blood supply to part of the brain is interrupted by a clot or a burst vessel. Clot-busting drugs given within hours of onset can reduce disability.
